title: View of Iudea (Ayutthaya), Capital of Siam / Gezicht op Iudea, de hoofdstad van Siam
artist: Attributed to the workshop of Johannes Vingboons (Vinckboons)
border: Oil/gouache painting on canvas; NO printed border or mount. Full-bleed image with only a faint painted sky margin; nothing needs trimming beyond optional edge crop.
fit: Outstanding colour bird's-eye veduta of the actual Siamese capital: the river-encircled island city with its grid of canals, gilded chedis and prangs, hills behind. The single strongest colour illustration of a real Thai city found. Warm, muted period palette that would sit well beside the other painterly plates.

title: Afbeeldinge der stadt Iudiad, hooft des Conincrijk Siam (bird's-eye view of Ayutthaya)
collection: Nationaal Archief, The Hague — Atlas of Mutual Heritage (AMH-5626-NA)
source: Wikimedia Commons, from Nationaal Archief / Atlas of Mutual Heritage
border: Hand-coloured pen-and-wash plan-view WITH margins, a titled Dutch caption strip along the top, and a visible horizontal join/seam across the sheet. Would need the caption strip and paper margins trimmed, and the seam is noticeable.
fit: Vivid hand-coloured plan-view of the same island city (greens, reds, gilded stupas). More cartographic/decorative than #1 but unmistakably Ayutthaya. Good back-up; slightly compromised by the seam and border text.

title: Bird's eye view of the city of Judia in Siam
collection: Nationaal Archief, The Hague — Atlas of Mutual Heritage (AMH-7236-KB)
source: Wikimedia Commons, from Nationaal Archief / Atlas of Mutual Heritage
border: Drawing with paper margins/border; muted, lightly-tinted palette (much less saturated than #1 and #2). Margins would need trimming.
fit: A third colour view of Ayutthaya, but the palette is pale/washed and it reads more as a tinted drawing. Weakest of the three; keep only as a fallback.
